traceability.notes:
Most of the story’s functional goals are implemented: - There is a dedicated ESLint rule (`prefer-implements-annotation`) that detects legacy `@story` + `@req` usage and emits recommendations. - The rule includes a conservative auto-fix that converts a single @story with one or more simple @req lines into a single @implements line, preserving formatting and order. - Multi-story and mixed @story/@req/@implements patterns are detected and reported without auto-fix. - @implements output conforms to the existing validation logic, and tests exercise the main behaviors. - A migration guide (docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md) documents the rule, auto-fix behavior, and configuration.
However, at least two important aspects of the specification are not satisfied: 1) Default severity / backward compatibility (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY and Definition of Done "Rule disabled by default"): - The story and docs clearly state the rule must be disabled by default (severity "off") to avoid changing behavior for existing users. - In the actual plugin exports, `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` is included in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES with value "warn", and that mapping is used for both `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict`. - This means that any consumer using the plugin’s recommended config will have the migration rule enabled by default, contradicting the specification. 2) Edge-case behavior for `@req` without `@story`: - The implementation notes specify that `@req` without a matching `@story` should be detected and warned as a non-auto-fixable case. - The current implementation simply ignores comments where either @story or @req is missing (`if (!hasStory || !hasReq) { return; }`), so this specific pattern does not produce the intended warning.
Because the published default configuration does not honor the required default-off behavior, and at least one described edge case is not handled as specified, the story is not fully implemented. Status: FAILED.
